gutman.name: Kasper Gutman
gutman.note: Drugged Holmes last night at the Hopkins Institute. Waiting for La Paloma.

brigid.name: Brigid O'Shaughnessy
brigid.note: Everyone is looking for her. She had the bird in Hong Kong.

cairo.name: Joel Cairo
cairo.note: Drinks at the Belvedere, smells of gardenia, and is afraid of Gutman.

CHAPTER.title: Chapter V · The Gunsel
CHAPTER.opening: Slowly, Watson. Look in the shop windows, not behind us.
intro: San Francisco. Wednesday, the day before La Paloma is due.
The fog came in at dawn and has not lifted.
Holmes has a telegram to send, and a fancy to walk to the telegraph office himself.
Up Kearny Street, Watson, and slowly. Let us see who else is taking the air this morning.
CHAPTER.summary: Gutman drugged Holmes at the Hopkins Institute to keep him away until La Paloma docks tomorrow. This morning Holmes walks up Kearny Street to send a telegram to Hong Kong.

paloma.title: La Paloma
paloma.text: From Hong Kong, due at the Pacific Mail wharf tomorrow. Gutman drugged me to keep me away until then.

reflection.title: In the jeweller's glass
reflection.text: Among the rings and watches, a reflection: a cap, an overcoat too good for its wearer, twenty paces back on the far side. When I stop, he stops.

sentinel.title: Kelly: since dawn
sentinel.text: The boy stood across from the Palace from six this morning, and asked the bell boy whether a lady had called on Mr. Holmes.

dollar.title: Kelly: a dollar
dollar.text: The boy paid Kelly a dollar to say which way Holmes went.

wire.title: The telegram
wire.text: To the harbour master, Hong Kong: "La Paloma. Who shipped cargo aboard her in November? A lady?" Sent from the Western Union on Kearny Street.

chances.title: Within reach
chances.text: He passed within a yard of my doorway with two guns in his pockets and never looked in. He was not sent to kill me.

register.title: The note for 12C
register.text: Left in the Alexandria's key box for Suite 12C, and read upside down across the desk: "H. walked to the telegraph office. No lady. Still looking. W."

CONCLUSION.question: Why is Gutman having Holmes followed?

answers.a: To kill him when the moment comes
answers.reply: He had his moment in the doorway, and a dozen before it. No.
Cairo is in the Belvedere's bar every night. Gutman need not follow me to find him.

answers.a: To keep him away from the wharf
answers.reply: Then the boy would be at the wharf, not on Kearny Street.

answers.a: To find Miss O'Shaughnessy, and through her the bird
answers.reply: "No lady. Still looking." He thinks she will come to me, and he wants to be there when she does.

epilogue: So the boy goes back to his master with nothing.
With a note that says so. Gutman will be impatient tonight, and impatient men make mistakes.
Tomorrow La Paloma comes in. Let us be on the wharf before any of them.

followed.title: Followed since dawn
followed.text: The boy took up his post outside the Palace at six and has walked behind me ever since. Gutman put him there.

watching.title: Watched, not hunted
watching.text: Two guns, a yard away, and he never touched them. His orders are to watch me, not to kill me.

lady.title: Gutman is looking for Brigid
lady.text: He asked whether a lady had called on me, and his report says "no lady. Still looking." Gutman thinks I will lead him to Miss O'Shaughnessy.

bought.title: Gutman buys what he needs
bought.text: A dollar for a constable, a whisky for a detective. Everyone has a price, to Gutman; it is the one thing he believes.

wired.title: Who shipped it
wired.text: When the harbour master answers, we shall know who put a parcel aboard La Paloma. I think I know already.

lines: Holmes steps into the hatter's doorway, among the hat boxes.
Twenty seconds later the boy goes by. Close enough to touch his sleeve. He never looks in.
Now, Watson, we follow him. Keep him in sight. When he looks back, be behind something.
The boy goes up the steps of the Alexandria without a look behind him.
At the desk he writes a note, folds it twice, and leaves it in the box for Suite 12C.
Suite 12C. Let us see what he has to report.

watson.name: Dr. Watson
watson.note: Liked Archer more than he will say. Takes people at their word, which is why I keep him by me.

kelly.name: Patrolman Kelly
kelly.note: Moved off Bush Street onto Kearny: his sergeant's idea of a kindness. Honest, mostly.

wilmer.name: Wilmer
wilmer.note: He has followed Holmes since dawn. Now Holmes follows him.

wilmer: New shoes, cheap: hired, not trusted
Right hand never leaves the pocket
kelly: Wet to the knees again: walked the beat all night
A new silver dollar in his tunic pocket
watson: Hasn't looked behind him once: good man

SPOTS.label: Step into the hatter's doorway
SPOTS.early: A hatter. I have hats enough, Watson.

SPOTS.say: The cabmen are asleep on their boxes. Nobody is going anywhere fast in this fog.
The Palace: eight hundred rooms, and the boy has watched the door of mine since six.

SPOTS.label: Look down Sutter Street
SPOTS.say: Sutter Street, Watson: the cable runs under the road all the way out to Larkin. Listen for the bell.
Oysters at ten in the morning. San Francisco never sleeps, it only lies down for an hour or two.

spotted: He saw me. He walks on, but he knows. Back, and try again.
Too close, Watson. He has us. Again.
lost: Gone, into the fog. Back to where we last had him.
Lost him. Again, and closer this time.

topics.q: What does Gutman want with me, Watson?
a: The bird, presumably. He thinks you know where it is.
Or he thinks I know someone who does.

topics.q: Why a telegram to Hong Kong?
a: Somebody put a parcel aboard La Paloma in November, Watson. Harbour masters keep books.

hello: Mr. Holmes! They've moved me off Bush Street onto Kearny. The sergeant's idea of a kindness.

topics.q: Have you seen a young man in a cap?
a: The little fellow in the good overcoat? Stood across from the Palace since six this morning, sir. Asked the bell boy if a lady had called on you.
Told me to mind my own business, sir. That was all.

challenge.tell: Kelly reddens, and his hand goes to his tunic pocket.
right: ...He gave me a dollar to tell him which way you went, sir. I told him up Kearny. I'm sorry, sir.
(He told him the truth, then. No matter: today I want to be followed.)
wrong: That was all, sir. Good day to you.
